nodes.summary: Let $d$ be a positive integer. For $P\in C_d(\mathbb Q)$ with $\delta_d(P)=(\alpha,\beta)$, let $s(P)=(r(\alpha),r(\beta))\in\mathbb Z^2$ be the pair of squarefree representatives. Then the x-form of the covering $D_{s(P)}$ holds over $\mathbb Q$, and $s(P)\in\mathrm{Sel}_2(C_d)$. For $P,Q\in C_d(\mathbb Q)$ (and any natural number $d$), $s(P)=s(Q)$ if and only if $\delta_d(P)=\delta_d(Q)$.

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field with $2\ne0$ and $d\in K^\times$. Then $\delta_d(P+Q)=\delta_d(P)\,\delta_d(Q)$ for all $P,Q\in C_d(K)$, so $\delta_d$ is a group homomorphism $C_d(K)\to(K^\times/K^{\times2})^2$. Moreover $\delta_d(2P)=1$ for every $P\in C_d(K)$, so $2C_d(K)$ lies in its kernel.
nodes.title: The complete 2-descent map is a homomorphism

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field with $2\ne0$ and $d\in K^\times$, and let $k(P)=(k_1(P),k_2(P))\in K\times K$ be the Kummer map of the coverings of $C_d$: $(1,1)$ at $O$; $(-1,-d)$, $(d,2)$, $(-d,-2d)$ at $(0,0)$, $(d,0)$, $(-d,0)$; and $(x,x-d)$ at every other point $(x,y)$. Then for every $P\in C_d(K)$ both $k_1(P)$ and $k_2(P)$ are nonzero, and $\delta_d(P)$ is the pair of their square classes.
nodes.title: The descent map is the Kummer map of the coverings

Then for every $(a,b)\in\mathrm{Sel}_2(C_d)$ the x-form of the covering $D_{a,b}$ holds over $\mathbb Q$.
